question.text: What is the value of e (Euler's number) used in the continuous compounding formula for theoretical futures price?

explanation.text: The Logic: e (Euler's number) is approximately 2.71828 and is the base of the natural logarithm. It is used in the theoretical futures price formula F = S x e^((r-rf)xt) and also appears as the exponential function in the option-pricing formulas covered in the workbook. The Trap: 3.14159 is pi, 1.41421 is the square root of 2, and 2.30259 is the natural log of 10 — none of these are the base of the natural exponential function used in continuous compounding. Note: Workbook references — p.64 (theoretical futures price formula with e = 2.71828) and pp.78-79 (e as the exponential function in option-pricing formulas).
